name: General business
description: The fallback for any business with no specific playbook. It still asks about the offer, the proof and the one action that brings customers, and it builds a full site, not four pages.

goals.prompt: What should the website do for your business? Name the one or two results that matter most.
goals.why: Every page and call to action is planned around these results.

recommendation.statement: Show proof that makes a stranger trust the business enough to get in touch

goals.reason: The usual two jobs of a business website.

audience.prompt: Who are your best customers, and what do they need to know before they contact you? One per line; add if known: wants: ... | proof: ... | action: ... | from: ... | mood: ...
audience.why: The pages answer the questions this person has, in the order they ask them.

recommendation.segment: People looking for what the business offers nearby or online
recommendation.need: Understand the offer, see proof, and know how to get started

audience.reason: A safe starting audience; research in P2 refines it.

trustSignals.label: A guarantee you can stand behind

heroMustHave: A headline that says what the business does and for whom, not its name alone
A real image of the business at work or its product, never generic stock

pages.title: Home
pages.purpose: Say what the business does and for whom, show proof, and lead the visitor to the main action

pages.title: Services
pages.purpose: Explain each service in plain words with who it is for and what the customer gets

pages.title: About
pages.purpose: Show who is behind the business and why customers can trust them

pages.title: Our Work
pages.purpose: Show real results with photographs and short case studies

pages.title: Contact
pages.purpose: Make contacting the business effortless, with the form, phone, address and hours

pages.title: How It Works
pages.purpose: Take away the fear of starting by showing each step from first call to finished job

pages.title: Customer Reviews
pages.purpose: Let customers speak, with names and details where they agree

pages.title: Questions Answered
pages.purpose: Answer the questions that stop people from contacting the business

pages.title: Pricing
pages.purpose: Set expectations on cost with honest ranges and what changes the price

pages.title: Our Team
pages.purpose: Put faces and credentials to the people who will do the work

pages.title: Insights
pages.purpose: Publish useful guidance that brings in people searching before they are ready to buy

pages.title: Careers
pages.purpose: Attract good people with the culture, the roles and a way to apply

pages.title: Service Areas
pages.purpose: Show where the business works, so local searchers know they are covered

questions.prompt: List what you sell or the services you provide, most important first.
questions.why: Each main offer gets its own section and the first one leads the home page.
questions.reason: Cannot be guessed; the site is built around it.

questions.prompt: In one sentence, why should a customer choose you over the competition?
questions.why: This becomes the home hero promise.
questions.reason: A real differentiator cannot be guessed.

questions.prompt: Where do you serve customers: one location, a city, a region or online?
questions.why: It decides whether the site leads with a local promise and a map.

options.label: A region or the whole country

questions.reason: Most small businesses serve a local area.

questions.prompt: How should the site talk about price?
questions.why: Hiding price loses some customers; showing it loses others.

options.label: Ask them to request a quote

questions.reason: The safe default when the price depends on the job.

questions.prompt: Which of these do you already have?
questions.why: Real photographs and proof make the site credible; the missing ones are made or sourced.

options.label: Photographs of the business, product or work
Videos of the business or work

questions.reason: The minimum a credible site needs.

questions.prompt: Where should enquiries go, and who follows them up?
questions.why: The main form and the call to action are wired to this.

questions.prompt: Name two or three competitors or sites you admire.
questions.why: Research studies them so the site is better where it counts.

/: hero with a clear promise, the primary action and one real image
the main services in plain words
proof: reviews, years in business or results
how it works in three steps
/contact: a map when there is a location

contentNeeds: Photographs of the business or work
List of services with a short description of each
Phone number, address and opening hours
compliance: Every number, year, guarantee or award must come from the client with a source

extras.note: Real photographs of the work are the strongest proof a small business has.
A short loop of the business at work adds life if the audience has decent connections.
Only worth adding when the business sells one recognisable physical object.
